risks.description: Pitching automation or AI services to an IT managed service provider whose business model includes selling low-code automation and AI agent design risks damaging ForgeX's credibility.

discovery.outreachSubject: Partnership inquiry / Capacity support for Microsoft Power Platform builds
discovery.outreachBody:
Hi [First Name],

I was reviewing Stability Networks' work in the Treasure Valley and noted your dedicated offerings around Microsoft Power Platform and Copilot Studio agent builds.

At ForgeX, we develop fixed-scope workflow automations and pipeline connectors. Rather than pitching internal tools that your engineers can easily build yourselves, we wanted to see if your team ever uses specialized subcontracting support when client demand for Power Platform or custom integration work exceeds your internal bench capacity.

If exploring a white-label or overflow development partnership makes sense, I would be glad to share our delivery model.

Best regards,

[Founder Name]
ForgeX
[Postal Address]
Opt-out: Reply with 'unsubscribe' to be immediately removed from all future correspondence.

qualification.rationale: Per the founder's explicit guidelines: 'Existing software capabilities should always be evaluated before recommending custom development' and 'The better answer may be that the company does not need ForgeX or already owns the necessary solution.' Stability Networks is a mature Managed IT and Cybersecurity provider with over 20 years of experience, 200+ customers, and an in-house engineering team that already specializes in Microsoft Power Platform, SharePoint automation, and Microsoft Copilot Studio AI agents. They already sell and deploy the same automation and AI agent services that ForgeX offers. Selling end-user automation packages to them is not viable; at most, only a potential subcontractor/overflow relationship could exist.
